#3606. Hacker Threatens To Leak Free Version Of GTA 6 In Crypto Grift

Somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap.

"It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them.

This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were quickly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme.

While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to issue a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

#3604. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

#3603. GTA 6 Is A British Success Story, Prime Minister Says, But He Won’t Play It

The Prime Minister of the UK, Andy Burnham, has labeled Rockstar Games a "British success story" amid GTA 6's rave reviews and huge sales milestones.

A spokesperson for his office told The Independent, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait."

Rockstar North is based in Edinburgh, Scotland, but GTA 6 was made by thousands of people across the globe. GTA is also historically linked to the UK, as the original game, 1997's Grand Theft Auto, was made by DMA Design in Edinburgh.

Asked if the PM himself would play GTA 6, his office said Burnham is too busy right now. "He won't be playing it," the spokesperson said.

GTA 6 launched on November 19 and reportedly sold nearly 25 million copies and earned $2 billion in revenue by launch day. The game boasts a mightily impressive 99 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic, meaning it's tied with the original Ocarina of Times for the highest aggregate review score for any game ever.

GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

#3602. 'Law & Order's E.J. Carroll Dies Suddenly at 66 While Traveling to New Job

Law & Order and Boardwalk Empire actor E.J. Carroll died unexpectedly while en route to a voiceover job. He was 66.

Carroll’s manager, Jon Mason, confirmed on Saturday, November 21, that the veteran character actor collapsed on the street in New York City on Thursday, November 19, while on his way to record lines for an upcoming commercial, per Entertainment Weekly.

A cause of death has not been determined. Mason noted that Mason had recently undergone a medical procedure to correct a hernia.

A memorial service will be held in New York City at a later date.

“When E.J. Carroll performed, it was impossible to take your eyes off him,” Mason said on Saturday. “But his lasting legacy will be the kindness and generosity he showed his friends, fellow performers and even strangers.”

Mason added that Carroll was “as good a human being as it gets.”

Us has reached out to Carroll’s representative for further information but did not hear back at the time of publication.

Carroll made his TV acting debut in 1998 via a guest spot in the original Law & Order. This brief appearance began a longstanding relationship that saw Carroll play at least seven characters across Law & Order and its spinoffs, Criminal Intent and Special Victims Unit.

He appeared in two episodes of acclaimed HBO crime drama Boardwalk Empire as the crooked Sheriff Victor Sickles, in addition to starring in six episodes of porn industry drama The Deuce as shop owner Fat Mooney.

Throughout his career, Carroll made guest appearances in hit shows such as Pose, Blue Bloods, The Blacklist, Damages and The Punisher. He appeared on the big screen in Golden Globe-winning sports drama The Wrestler and holiday ensemble Everybody’s Fine.

“I think what makes an actor good is doing your homework, first of all, and you really have to love it,” Carroll said on a July 2024 episode of the “On Acting” podcast. “I still love it more than anything. … Even if I’m doing a little commercial or something, I still [do research and make up a backstory].”

His manager revealed that Carroll completed work on Delicate Arrangement, a film about the true story of Gone With the Wind actress Vivien Leigh‘s unlikely friendship with a blue-collar florist. The movie will feature Spy Kids alum Carla Gugino as Leigh and Stranger Things star Matthew Modine as the florist.

“I had the great fortune of working with E.J. last winter in Philadelphia,” Gugino, 55, told Entertainment Weekly in a statement. “He was a source of talent and light. My deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. RIP E.J.”

SPOILERS AHEAD for The End of Oak Street, now streaming with a HBO Max subscription.

One of the biggest “shock” sounds I’ve made while in a movie theater this year has been for The End of Oak Street. I knew the Spielberg-inspired science fiction movie would have dinosaurs and probably some wild twists, but I really wasn’t expecting Greg’s death. I just found out that what happens after the dino chomps him up was originally much different.

The End of Oak Street feels like one of those rare family-oriented sci-fi flicks we don’t see enough anymore. So, I was very surprised when Ewan McGregor’s character dies in front of his wife and kids. It was completely heartbreaking to watch – especially right after that kinky dino scene. It really darkened the tone of the whole movie. But, as it turns out, it was originally even darker. Crazy, right? As Anne Hathaway revealed to Entertainment Weekly:

Greg always died in the script, but in the original movie that I signed up for, he didn’t come back. And that was something that got changed very close to the start of filming. I have to give all credit to David and J.J. because they had total faith that it was the right thing to do. And they kept turning to me and I was like, ‘Guys, I was so invested in the other version. I have no way of knowing this. I’m just trusting you that this is the right thing to do.’

Now, I didn’t think Greg was going to come back when I watched the movie, because how could he? Once what’s left of the Platt family goes through the portal and realises they’ve travelled back in time, I was so happy with what happened next. Denise calls her husband to deliver a pizza, and he does just in time to be outside the radius of Oak St.

Sure, the logic for the ending is a tad janky, but I needed that feel-good conclusion (along with the dog not dying either, of course). To me, the movie is only about dinosaurs on the surface. The more interesting part is the dynamic between the Platt family. At the beginning of it, Denise and Greg are clearly having some marital problems, and Denise feels resentful and stagnant with her husband. But they start to find their way back to each other while in crisis. And then she sees him take charge of their family by defending them – even though he sadly dies in the process. It’s the weird, twisted sci-fi family therapy they somehow all needed.

Hathaway has also shared her love of the ending of The End of Oak Street, too. In her words:

When I saw the movie, I saw it with someone who had lost their father, and they burst into tears at the ending. They said, ‘Actually, it’s just what I want from a movie like this, and it could only happen in a movie, and I love it.’ And so I just want to give my absolute credit and hats off to J.J. and David for coming up with that ending.

Sure, characters often need to die in movies, but not in this one. I love Hathaway’s anecdote about how Greg coming back to life positively affected one viewer. The ending adds a bit of wish fulfilment and helps even out the tone of the whole experience. Look, if the end is going to include two Jeannettes by the end, Greg can live too! I'm so happy he did.

#3598. GTA 7? Please, Let GTA 6 Cook First, Take-Two CEO Says

Rockstar Games just launched Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales. Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon.

Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a new GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world."

Zelnick, for his part, said people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7.

"I can't help myself. We at Take-Two just went live GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7," he said.

While Rockstar isn't talking about GTA 7 yet--and no one should expect that to happen anytime soon--Take-Two has already signaled that the next GTA game could come out sooner.

He said the “nature and velocity” of the company’s content releases in its major franchises, including GTA, will look “dramatically different over the next decade.”

GTA 6 released more than 13 years after GTA 5 came out in 2013. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously.

The evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

As the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director said, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”

L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she said. She then welcomed the company’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone showed up and showed out,” she said, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance company with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

During a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she said. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

#3595. GTA 6 Doesn’t Have Any Doja Cat Music, And She Didn’t Censor Her Message To Rockstar

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now, and the game features a lot of music from famous real-world artists. But Doja Cat is not among them.

She's not happy about that, either.

Doja Cat said online that she is "so f**kin bitter" about that. In follow-up posts, she told Rockstar to "eat my d**k." She said she loves GTA 6, and being left out of the game breaks her heart. Directing her posts at Rockstar in this way, with this language, is unlikely to win her any fans at the studio, so it would be surprising indeed if we see her music get added to the game at any point.

Doja Cat's music is not on any of GTA 6's in-game radio stations, nor do any of her tunes feature on the 34-song GTA 6: The Album, which is out now. The album includes music from Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Morgan Wallen, Young Thug, Cardi B, Keith Richards, Lana Del Rey, and more.

The in-game radio stations, meanwhile, feature music from Tom Petty, George Strait, Glen Campbell, Bad Bunny, Drake, Lil Wayne, Slayer, Sepultura, System of a Down, and Tool, just to name few.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you're eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3594. All of These Nebula Projectors Are up to $700 Off Ahead of Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Black Friday is still a couple of weeks away, with the big shopping event falling on November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3593. GTA 6 Is Crashing On Some PS5s With CE-108255-1 Error Code

After years of waiting, GTA fans can finally play GTA 6, but some players are encountering a dreaded error code that makes the game crash or otherwise fail.

Users are reporting receiving the CE-108255-1 error code, which players might see when a game crashes mid-session or fails to load entirely. Crashing mid-game in GTA 6 would be particularly frustrating given how saves work.

Sony's official word is that players can try updating their game to fix the issue. If it's really that simple, that would be a welcome result. But people are saying that doesn't always work and are asking Rockstar to put out an official patch.

Reddit user Acrobatic-Promise458 encountered this issue and documented their experience. The person said the game was working normally until they reached a certain point in the story, at which point the game crashes continually. They said Rockstar support directed them to Sony's own support team, but it was no use.

People online (via Gizmodo) are theorizing that the crashing issues with GTA 6 on PS5 might be due to the game's intense demands on the hardware, and it could be specifically tied to older PS5s.

Rockstar has yet to officially respond to these reports. Rockstar's official GTA 6 error troubleshooting page isn't much help, as it only links to the support sites for PlayStation and Xbox and offers no specific help. Players can submit a support ticket to Rockstar to get more help with this issue or others.

These issues do not appear to be very widespread, but if you're experiencing the CE-108255-1 error on PS5, that's no consolation to you.

GTA 6 has reportedly sold 25 million copies and earned more than $2 billion in revenue already, and those numbers are only expected to grow higher.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

In the world of celebrity fashion, trends that involve sheer clothes, corsets and even things like chainmail are very popular. They’re iconic, and many celebs have shared their unique takes on them. Recently, I’ve seen a few people jump on a totally different trend, though: “Bird.” Yes, you read that right: birds are a new red carpet fad, and we can thank Rosalía and a few of the newest Hunger Games stars for it.

Earlier this week, Whitney Peak made waves when she wore a gown to the premiere of the book-to-screen adaptation of Sunrise on the Reaping that featured a white bird flying off her shoulder. The gorgeous blue Robert Wun gown and that white bird that got in Jesse Plemons way really got people talking. And then, a few days later, Rosalía showed up to the Los40 Music Awards wearing this:

Fittingly, this dress is by the same designer who made Peak’s gown, per W. The lovely white dress and the white bird fascinator are from Robert Wun’s fall 2026 couture collection. And hilariously enough, Peak’s dress originally had two birds, one being a fascinator on the model’s head and the other being attached to her shoulder.

Luke Meagher pointed this out on Instagram too, as he wondered why Peak only had one of the two birds her dress had when it was featured on a runway. He also explained that the birds could have gotten separated because Rosalía seemingly had the other one. In response to all that, the Sunrise on the Reaping actress took to her IG story to repost the video about the two birds and write:

Well, we did get them, and now I’d like to see where these birds pop up next. Clearly, they’re a hot commodity and a lovely fashion statement.

However, I’d like to point out that these are not the only two bird-themed looks we’ve seen this week.

At the same event where Peak wore her gown with the flying bird, her Sunrise on the Reaping co-star, Mckenna Grace, also donned a dress with big bird energy. Well, I should say big Mockingjay energy. That’s because, to close out her iconic run of Hunger Games-themed outfits, she wore a dress that resembled the winged gown Katniss wore in Catching Fire and featured full-sized, feather-covered wings that ran down her arms.

So, clearly, birds are having a moment on the red carpet. Now, as we close out the 2026 movie schedule, I’ll be curious to see if other celebs hop on this trend. Clearly, it's a stunning one, as Peak, Rosalía and Grace all made big splashes with their outfits, and I’d be so curious to see how other celebs can work birds into their red carpet fits.

#3591. ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Francis Lawrence on the Film’s Final Scene

When Francis Lawrence, the filmmaker behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, greets me over Zoom, he’s aware that his darkly lit, gothic backdrop makes him look a bit like the villainous President Snow. “All I need is a big eagle back here,” the white-haired, smartly dressed director jokes.

Lawrence has helmed almost every film in Lionsgate’s blockbuster series, based on Suzanne Collins’s best-selling novels about a dystopia where a bloodthirsty dictator forces children to fight to the death for the elite’s entertainment. He joined the franchise for its 2013 sequel, Catching Fire, and has directed only three non–Hunger Games movies in the decade-plus since. In that time, one could argue, the world has tilted further toward the oppressive future depicted in Collins’s novels—see, for instance, Donald Trump’s Hunger Games–esque Patriot Games. And while Lawrence isn’t naming names, he’s never lost sight of the movies’ larger political message. “I feel really lucky to be able to tell stories that matter, that are wrapped in these commercial packages,” he tells Vanity Fair. “So anytime one of these things comes around, I jump at it.”

Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the new movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada. He plays the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch Abernathy, a victor of the Hunger Games who later serves as a mentor to actor Lawrence’s Katniss Everdeen. Making a reflective movie prompted director Lawrence to reflect on his own Hollywood trajectory. “The biggest difference is that I’m a lot more relaxed. I was nervous as hell on Catching Fire,” he says. “It was my fourth movie. It was a movie I was inheriting. It was a big movie, and it was a massive cast. So I was really intimidated. Now I have much more fun, I will say. I’m much more comfortable with actors, and the amount of actors, and with logistics. And there’s definitely a family that’s built into it, which is very important for me. There’s, what, 14 years of my life spent making these movies? So it has to be fun.”

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: When did you become aware of Sunrise on the Reaping, and at what point did you and Suzanne Collins start discussing an adaptation?

Francis Lawrence: When we did the original series of movies, and we finished the last Mockingjay, she said she was done, and we thought that was it. Then she surprised me and Nina [Jacobson], the producer, with Ballad, however many years later. And she never tells us when she’s writing. Even when she has something to read, she never tells us what it’s about. She’s very superstitious about it all. So we got the call, which was very exciting. And she said, “Go to my agent’s house. There’s a manuscript. Let’s talk after you read it.”

I got to his house, sat in his backyard, and there was a manuscript and a copy of Catching Fire sitting on top of it with a few tabs in it. I opened to the tabs and saw that it had the portion where Katniss and Peeta were looking up the Haymitch Games, that sequence from the book. And I was like, Oh, she’s written the Haymitch story, which was very exciting. And that started the process that we always have, which is that I read the manuscript in one sitting, then read it a second time after having a conversation with Suzanne.

Then I fly to New York and meet her at Scholastic, and we sit up in a conference room for about a week going through the book, beat by beat, of what we think the movie is going to be. She and I lay it all out and chat, and she sits on her computer and writes a scriptment. Then that’s the thing that we turn over to the screenwriter.

How have you built that trust with the author of these books, having adapted them for more than a decade now?

That working process happened accidentally when I signed on to do Catching Fire. I had never done a sequel to someone else’s first movie before. And when Lionsgate and the first director, [Gary Ross], parted ways and I got the call, they didn’t have a script, but they had started the process of developing it before I was on board. And so I signed on based on the book and had planned a trip to New York to meet with Suzanne.

The script came on the day that I was traveling to New York. I read it, and it was not the movie that I wanted to make—because I loved the book, and it was not the book. Luckily, nobody else wanted to make that version of the movie either. Our meeting of me just picking her brain turned into, “This script doesn’t work. Let’s go through, page by page, and figure out the version of the movie we want to make.”

That’s what really formed the bond—just working really, really closely with her. Spending 8 or 10 hours a day for a week or two in a conference room—me riffing on visual ideas and her talking about the story. We think the same way in terms of storytelling, structure, and she seemed to take to my visual ideas.

There’s this weird dynamic that happens as we get closer to production. We’re usually developing the script pretty much within a week of shooting. But the production is also building. So you have thousands of people working, figuring out locations, traveling in different parts of the world. The stress levels are building.

Suzanne and I have related the relationship to almost like a mother-son relationship. It starts really lovely and creative, but then as we get closer and closer, it’s me being that late teen who’s ready to leave the home, like, Okay, enough’s enough. I’m going to go make the movie now. I have to say, I love the process. It’s not without its stress sometimes, but that’s part of the closeness of it all that I cherish.

How did this film’s futuristic-meets-1970s aesthetic come about?

There was an element [of the story] that reminded me a bit of Alice in Wonderland, which then made me think of Jefferson Airplane, that song “White Rabbit,” which brought me to the ’60s and ’70s. Then you can look at characters certain ways. Like, Haymitch, you go, Okay, he’s from, like, young Bruce Springsteen, or Lenore Dove [played by Whitney Peak], like a young Stevie Nicks. And you get this hippie vibe. And the Capitol is that Warhol Studio 54 crowd, and Snow like a ’70s Yves Saint Laurent.

How do you go about casting a young Haymitch, finding an actor who can anchor the film like Jennifer Lawrence did in the original Hunger Games film?

Our casting director, Deb Zane, had met him, and I want to say before he did East of Eden. She had a lot of faith in him. We liked his self-tape a lot. But we knew that he was going to have to pull a lot off. He starts as a very optimistic, fun, playful, young guy in love, and in this movie has to turn into somebody that’s much closer to the Haymitch that we’re used to—cynical and a drunk. He’s going to have to go through a lot of emotional trauma, plus have that kind of mischievousness, irreverence, all these different elements that Woody [Harrelson] has naturally. And so we really put him through the ringer. We did a lot of tests, kept bringing him back, bringing him back, bringing him back. He and I were modulating how much Woody we feel in his performance.

I want to make sure that everybody makes the role their own. That they find the spirit of the character and that it’s not trying to do an imitation of somebody. That’s true of Elle [Fanning] doing Effie, of Ralph [Fiennes] doing Snow, of Jesse [Plemons] doing Plutarch, Kieran [Culkin] as Caesar. Everybody has to figure out how to do it on their own. Then the weird thing is that Kelvin [Harrison Jr., who plays a young Beetee], has worked with Jeffrey [Wright] three times. So he’s fairly close with Jeffrey. When he got the role, he called and said, “You won’t believe this, but I’m actually playing the young version of you.” He could just conjure Jeffrey Wright. His voice, the speech patterns, the timbre of the sound of everything. It was pretty wild.

Were there storylines from the previous films that you felt you could plant Easter eggs for? I’m thinking specifically of the romantic chemistry between Effie and Haymitch.

There are certain Capitol characters where I give a lot of freedom for improvisation. Effie, Caesar, Drusilla [played by Glenn Close], there’s a lot of room for ad-libs. One of the elements that we definitely played with a bit came from an improvised moment in the [last] Mockingjay. We were shooting this scene in Atlanta outside of Snow’s mansion, which is one of the very last scenes of Katniss in the Capitol. She’s saying goodbye to Effie, and then Haymitch and Effie kiss.

Quite honestly, it was an idea because Woody just wanted to kiss Elizabeth Banks. But everybody thought it would be fun and that the fans would dig it, that Haymitch kissed her. Then it became this big thing of this hidden love that Haymitch and Effie have for one another. And Elle played into that a bit. So there’s, I would say, a hint of flirtation here between the two, less so on Haymitch’s side. His heart is obviously somewhere else in the story. But Elle definitely brought a bit of that to it. That was not scripted. That’s the fun of having great actors.

What was it like to reunite Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson from the original movies?

Jen and I have stayed close over the years. We’ve done four movies together. Josh, who basically has moved to Spain, I haven’t seen in a long time. Woody I see off and on and text every once in a while. But there was something really special about the three of them being back together.

It’s also really, for the most part, the same crew from 2012, when we started making Catching Fire. It’s the same DP [Jo Willems], the same camera operator [David J. Thompson], the same AD [Christopher Surgent].

[When] they got to the hotel, Jen and Josh were in the bar having a beer or something, and I was like, Okay, I won’t even shower. I won’t get out of my rain gear. I’ll just come in. The next thing you know, there were 40 of us who had been together since Catching Fire, the gang back together. It’s like a high school reunion or something, but in the best possible way.

There’s a futility to what happens in this film, knowing where we end up in future movies. How do you handle that aspect of history being doomed to repeat itself?

Look, we’re doing a story where you know the lead character is going to make it out. It’s really about how he makes it out, and what he ends up being like at the end of it all. What I’m really pleased about is that the way Suzanne wrote the book, and the way I think we’ve ended the movie, there is a sense of hope that the tragedy is not for nothing. That was really important to me. And one of the beautiful elements in the story, which comes a bit later, is this sense of, everybody has to find their voice. Everybody has to participate.

It really deals with this thing that I think is happening a lot today, where you find apathy: people not wanting to vote, feeling even if they do vote that it’s not going to matter. This idea that you have to be active, and you can’t expect immediate gratification—that everybody needs to stand up and it may take generations, but you still have to do it.

Outside of my screening on the Upper West Side, there was a group protesting Elon Musk and data centers because the documentary about him was playing at the theater. It was a reminder that there will always be something to rise up against, and always people who will be willing to do it.

Yeah, exactly. And ideally, at some point, if everybody stands up, something will change.

During the 13 years that you’ve worked in this universe, dystopia has felt more and more familiar. How have real-world events influenced your filmmaking?

In the 56 years I’ve been alive, there’s never really been a time where I’ve felt like, Oh wow, everything is great. Nothing is wrong in the world. It always feels like there’s some dystopian sense about the world at any given time. And somehow Suzanne is always able to write these stories about it, which is what makes these movies feel timeless. A lot of people just see them as spectacles, but really they’re about our times very specifically. Almost in a subversive way, I feel like we’ve gotten to smuggle these ideas into these movies that a lot of people go see.

#3590. GTA 6’s Astonishing $4 Billion Day One Includes 32.5 Million Copies Sold

GTA 6 is an enormous hit--it's the biggest gaming release ever. Take-Two just announced that GTA 6 reach 32.5 million copies sold before release, with revenue reaching $3.79 billion through the end of the first day on sale on November 19. This makes it the biggest entertainment release--for any medium--in history, Take-Two said.

For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers. GTA 5 launched at $60, compared to $80 for the cheapest version of GTA 6.

For comparison, the all-time highest-grossing movie ever is Avengers: Endgame, which made $2.94 billion during its entire run. GTA 6 has done nearly $1 billion more in revenue already. According to reporter Jason Schreier, GTA 6 is also now instantly one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games
with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.”

Big numbers for GTA 6 were always expected. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch.

GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3588. GTA 6 Sets Even More Records

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release.

For starters, the internet service provider Comcast announced that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the company's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network.

GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast said around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the New Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said.

A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight.

Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster.

Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox.

These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

#3586. GTA 6 Has Dexter References, And Now Dexter Himself Has Reacted

Actor Michael C. Hall has reacted to how GTA 6 features references to his Miami-set TV show Dexter, in which he famously played the serial killer Dexter.

Appearing on the Barstool Movies show, Hall said he was "informed" of the Easter eggs in GTA 6 about his character. "I wasn't consulted," he said with a laugh. "It's pretty cool to feel like [Dexter] has folded into the zeitgeist."

After the GTA 6 Extended Look premiered in August, people immediately spotted what they thought was Dexter's apartment building from the TV show. Now that GTA 6 has arrived, people found the apartment building in the game, and you can, too, by following GameSpot's Dexter apartment guide here.

On the TV show, Dexter dismembers his victims, stuffs them into garbage bags, and dumps them into the nearby harbor on his boat, the Slice of Life.

Players can also get into a kill house that bears a resemblance to the one that Dexter uses on the show, complete with plastic sheets for the blood splatter, hammers, and cleavers. Players have also found bones underwater, presumably another reference to Dexter.

GTA 6 is full of Easter eggs, so be sure to check out GameSpot's breakdown of GTA 6's best Easter eggs to seek out while you're traveling around Vice City.

GTA 6 launched on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it sold more than 32 million copies and brought in close to $4 billion in revenue by day one.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

After Ariana Grande decided to take a break from public life for a little bit, she recently came back into the spotlight for the premiere of Focker-In-Law. Whether the starlet is out and about or not, though, her music consistently plays across the airwaves. So what's it like for Grande to hear her work in public? Well, the Wicked actress got real about the wildest place she heard her music, and believe me when I say I was not expecting her to mention a bikini wax while explaining.

With the former Nickelodeon actress being one of the best-selling artists of all time and having ten Billboard Top 100 singles, she gets a lot of airtime. So it's pretty much a given that Grande would hear her own music now and then. As a matter of fact, when Harper’s Bazaar asked Grande about the wildest place she ever heard her own songs, she mentioned a wax:

Yeah, I was one time getting a bikini wax. And the song came on, and I didn’t think [the bikini wax employee] knew who I was at all. I never assume that anyone does.

Grande continued to mimic the satisfied look of the wax specialist, who also said to her, “And my kids love your show!” While the former child has spoken before about how fame tends to complicate her music career, it looks like it can also come with some surreal and somewhat funny encounters with fans as well.

A celebrity like Hugh Jackman can relate to the joy of hearing his own music in public. Months after his movie, The Greatest Showman, premiered, he recalled overhearing the film’s soundtrack as he was making his way to the door of an apartment or hotel. I can imagine it feeling like such an honor for an artist when someone is enjoying their work in some form or another.

Let's also be real, as Ariana Grande’s music is easy to love, given her immense talent. Per a fun fact about Grande, five-time Grammy winner Gloria Estefan spotted her talent when she was 8 years old and singing on a cruise ship. I think it's fair to say Estefan knows talent when she sees it.

Thanks to Grande's four-octave range and songwriting skills, she knows how to make her music fun and catchy. Back in 2019, her single “Thank U, Next” broke an impressive record, as it surpassed Ed Sheeran and Cardi B.’s streaming sales. And, this year, the “Positions” singer’s Eternal Sunshine Tour was her second highest-grossing tour she’s had, earning $107.9 million.

Now, on the heels of that top-selling tour ended in, Grande can celebrate her role in the highly anticipated Focker-In-Law. The film sees Grande play the fiancée of Greg Focker’s son, who also ends up having a rivalry with her future father-in-law. It’ll be exciting to see “The Way” singer go back to her comedy roots and mix it up with stars like Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro.

I wonder whether Grande's music was played on set and if so, which tracks were selected. Personally, I think a set seems like a more obvious place for her to hear her songs as opposed to a place where she can get a bikini wax. That aside, check out the Oscar nominee in Focker-in-Law when it opens on November 25th amid the 2026 movie release.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3584. 10 Shows Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

What started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Plan on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole new persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

This is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Blending the Big Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

The tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

#3583. GTA 6 Players Captivated By Mandy Apparently Include A Former Nintendo President

A character named Mandy has the attention of many Grand Theft Auto 6 players--and that appears to include Reggie Fils-Aimé, the man who used to run Nintendo of America.

Per GamesRadar, former Nintendo marketing and public relations manager Krysta Yang joked on social media that GTA 6, which is front-loaded with a lot of simulation-like busywork in the first chapter, is "adult Animal Crossing," posting images that highlight parallels between GTA 6 and Animal Crossing: New Horizons. Fils-Aimé quoted the post, saying: "If so, where's Mandy?"

It's slightly eyebrow raising that the former executive for a family-friendly company like Nintendo seems to have a strong opinion for a rather promiscuous video game character. No judgment to Fils-Aimé, of course, but talk around Mandy carries a certain... tone. Minor spoilers for the early parts of GTA 6 follow.

One of the earliest missions in GTA 6 has Jason stopping by Mandy's home to collect rent. Long story short, she flirts pretty aggressively with Jason, who clearly isn't reciprocating, and Mandy doesn't take it well. And no, even if players wanted to, you can't romance Mandy.

It doesn't help that it's implied that Mandy carries a dark secret, with Jason discovering a severed finger while fixing her sink's pipes. I'm not sure if anyone in Animal Crossing is that shady.

So what does this post say about Reggie Fils-Aimé as a person? It's unclear what he thinks of the character--all we know is that he'd really like to know who the Animal Crossing equivalent of Mandy would be. It certainly wouldn't be Isabelle, so take your pick of any weird villagers you've encountered. Either way, it seems that Fils-Aimé is playing GTA 6 like the rest of us or, at the very least, is in tune with the massive cultural zeitgeist the game has produced.
